subsystems.name: Quantum processing unit
subsystems.role: holds the encoded problem state in a controllable quantum system.
parts: qubits (superconducting transmons, trapped ions, neutral atoms, photonics, or flux qubits in annealers)
dilution refrigerator or vacuum and laser system

subsystems.name: Problem encoding
subsystems.role: turns a business or engineering problem into a form the hardware can hold.

subsystems.name: Algorithm layer
subsystems.role: the quantum routine that searches the solution space.

subsystems.name: Classical control loop
subsystems.role: measures results and steers the quantum run.
parts: outer-loop optimiser tuning the circuit parameters

subsystems.name: Readout and error mitigation
subsystems.role: extracts a usable answer from a noisy device.
parts: decoding and sampling of candidate solutions

subsystems.name: Benchmarking
subsystems.role: decides whether the quantum run was actually better.
parts: best-in-class classical solvers for the same instance
instances chosen to be hard for classical heuristics

buildSteps.title: Formulate the problem
buildSteps.detail: State it in binary decision variables — routes chosen, jobs assigned, assets held — and write down the objective and constraints.

buildSteps.title: Map to a cost function
buildSteps.detail: Convert it into an Ising or QUBO energy function, adding penalty weights so that invalid answers cost more energy than valid ones.

buildSteps.title: Choose the hardware
buildSteps.detail: Annealing suits dense QUBO problems; gate-based machines need the search expressed as a short circuit of tens to thousands of gates.

buildSteps.title: Compile onto the device
buildSteps.detail: For annealers, map the problem graph onto the chip's sparse coupler graph (minor embedding). For gate machines, transpile the ansatz into native single- and two-qubit gates and respect the qubit connectivity.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure single- and two-qubit gate fidelities, coherence times (tens to hundreds of microseconds for superconducting qubits) and readout error; recalibrate between runs.

buildSteps.title: Run the hybrid loop
buildSteps.detail: Execute the circuit or annealing schedule, sample many shots, and feed the measured energies back to a classical optimiser that adjusts the parameters — hundreds of iterations per problem.

buildSteps.title: Decode and repair
buildSteps.detail: Translate bitstrings back into problem variables and fix constraint violations, often with a small classical routine.

buildSteps.title: Refine classically
buildSteps.detail: Feed the best quantum sample into a classical local search — the quantum device acts as a sampler, not the whole solver.

buildSteps.title: Benchmark honestly
buildSteps.detail: Compare against tuned classical heuristics on the same instances, at the same time budget, and report whether any real gap survives.

prerequisites.tech: Qubits with high two-qubit gate fidelity
prerequisites.why: gates near 99.9 % fidelity exist on leading platforms, but error accumulates as circuits lengthen.
problems rarely match a chip's coupler graph, so embedding costs extra qubits and can swamp small devices.
variational loops and error correction need feedback in microseconds; orchestration overhead often dominates run time.
logical qubits have been demonstrated but not at the thousands needed for reliably deep optimisation circuits.
mixed-integer and heuristic solvers are fast and improving, so any quantum advantage must beat a moving target.

pathway.milestone: NISQ-era experiments on small Max-Cut, scheduling and portfolio instances
pathway.unlocks: tooling, embeddings and benchmarking practice, but no demonstrated advantage at useful sizes.

pathway.milestone: application-specific benchmarks where quantum samplers match but do not beat the best classical methods
pathway.unlocks: clear picture of which problem structures might eventually favour quantum hardware.

pathway.milestone: error-mitigated runs on tens to hundreds of high-fidelity qubits with real-world constraint handling
pathway.unlocks: credible pilot use in logistics or finance alongside classical solvers.

pathway.milestone: fault-tolerant machines running quantum-walk or phase-estimation algorithms for structured search problems
pathway.unlocks: possible asymptotic speedups on specific optimisation families, still limited by input and output costs.
